system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
In which of these drawings is the dotted line a line of symmetry?

Figure, described in words:
Four line drawings labeled A, B, C, and D, each with a straight dotted line:
- A: A top-down view of a butterfly, tilted diagonally. The dotted line passes straight through the body from between the antennae to the tail, splitting the butterfly into two symmetric halves.
- B: A front-facing outline of a human body standing upright with arms at the sides. A horizontal dotted line passes across the waist.
- C: A front view of an elephant with its trunk curved slightly to one side, its tail visible on only one side, and asymmetric feet. A vertical dotted line runs down the center of the drawing.
- D: A snake drawn horizontally, stretched out with its head on the right and tail on the left. A vertical dotted line cuts across the snake's body near the middle.

A. [Image: Butterfly with a dotted line]
B. [Image: Outline of a human body with a dotted line]
C. [Image: Elephant with a dotted line]
D. [Image: Snake with a dotted line]

answer.description: The letter of the option you choose for the question.
